html:
A kingdom in what is now northeast China, the Russian Far East and northern Korea, from 698 to 926. The map shows it in 800; it appears again in 900 as Balhae, another spelling of the same name.

It was founded by Dae Joyeong, a former officer of Goguryeo, after the Tang and Silla had destroyed that kingdom. He led a mix of Goguryeo people and Mohe tribes to victory over Tang forces and set up his own state, first called Jin. Its rulers saw themselves as Goguryeo's heirs, and both Korea and China now claim its history.

Parhae soon made peace with the Tang and copied its ways: its capital at Sanggyeong was laid out like Chang'an. It traded furs, horses and ginseng, and sent more than thirty missions across the sea to Japan. To its south lay Unified Silla, a rival it seldom dealt with. Chinese writers called it the flourishing land in the east.
